sources.note: NC last resort for typical wild lifespan and mass range. ADW sections 'Physical Description' and 'Lifespan/Longevity'; it cites Mowbray (1999), Birds of North America. Checked permissive alternatives: USFWS page supplies length and wingspan but no mass or typical-lifespan statistic; USDA Forest Service account has no lifespan statistic. Smithsonian reports a rounded 2-3 year wild lifespan, but its terms reserve page content unless marked CC0, and the species page is not marked CC0. No checked permissive source gives the sex-specific average wild lifespan or the mass range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The ADW account directly reports typical wild lifespan 20.68-27.98 months and sex-specific means 1.7 y (female) and 2.3 y (male). Use their equal-weight arithmetic mean, 2.0 y, as a derived species value. The 21 y maximum is separate and was not used. NC-SA last resort; exact statistic is unavailable from checked permissive sources.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW behavior section says most activity occurs during the day.

behavior.note: USFWS supports feeding on submerged aquatic vegetation and land grazing, flushing when wary, and seasonal nocturnal feeding during hunting seasons. ADW supports the general pattern of daytime swimming/feeding. The program simplifies this to daylight activity/night rest, with no hunting-season state because the schema has no hunting-context trigger.

look.note: Judgement: stylized plumage palette and block proportions based on adult male/female physical descriptions.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of ADW adult mass range 665-1330 g, converted to kg: (0.665+1.330)/2 = 0.9975 kg. This is an authored typical-mass proxy, not a reported mean. Public USFWS page gives no mass value.

seasonal.phases.note: USFWS says nesting primarily in Canada and southward migration begins late August to early September, reaching winter grounds in Texas/Mexico and California. The broad absent window in Mexico and breeding window are authored month approximations.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, juvenile and adult are the generic life stages represented; no duration values are asserted.
